key_findings.finding: The requested transformation is most plausibly a Suzuki–Miyaura cross-coupling: the heteroaryl triflate is the electrophile and the aryl boronic acid, Cc1ccc2c(cnn2C2CCCCO2)c1B(O)O, supplies the aryl fragment. The expected product is the corresponding biaryl in which the C–B(OH)2 position is bonded to the aryl carbon formerly bearing O–SO2CF3; carbonate base and methanol are consistent with the stated coupling setup. The exact triflate/boronic-acid pair was not found as an exact ORD record, so the product assignment is structural interpretation rather than an exact database product record.

key_findings.finding: In the closest ORD Suzuki-like records for this boronic acid, the highest reported yield was 78.1% using palladium acetate plus tricyclohexylphosphine, with cesium carbonate, at 100 °C for 5 h. Triphenylphosphine records gave 77.4%, 76.5%, 76.3%, 76.2%, 75.1%, 74.2%, 73.7%, and 73.2% under the listed variants. Thus, among the provided ligand classes, the bulky alkyl phosphine category—specifically PCy3—is the ligand most directly associated with the highest-yielding retrieved reaction.
